roadmap_item: §5, area I: does M2h's one scale survive a split that cannot leak through shared compiled elements -- held out by CHROMOSOME, registered
question: M2h fitted ONE scale on training genes and read it on held-out genes, splitting by sha256 of the gene SYMBOL -- a RANDOM split -- and its multiplicative arm read 'better' (held-out Delta MSE +0.04339 [98.33% CI +0.0379, +0.04894], fitted scale +0.2146, about 2% of the variance, control p = 0.000999). Genes that share a compiled element are not independent, so a random split can leak: a training gene and a held-out gene may be fitted through the same element. Does the scale survive a split that CANNOT leak through shared elements -- held out by CHROMOSOME, which is disjoint in element membership -- with the scale REFITTED on the training chromosomes; and is the magnitude of the scale the same?
why_stronger: the compiler emits ONE PROGRAM PER CHROMOSOME and an element's target is chosen inside that program, so an element on chr7 can enter the rules of chr7 genes only. The 24 chromosomes are therefore DISJOINT IN ELEMENT MEMBERSHIP, and in a chromosome-held-out fold no training gene and no held-out gene can share a compiled element. A chromosome-held-out fit is a strictly stronger generalisation test of M2h's claim than its random split, on the same rows. The converse is the thing to keep in view: a chromosome split ALSO breaks regional structure that a random split preserves (replication timing, gene density, compartment, chromosome-specific gene families), so a drop between the two splits is evidence that M2h's number is not free of element-level leakage WITHOUT being proof that leakage is the whole of the difference. That distinction is registered here and is not softened afterwards

carried_verbatim.endpoint: y(G, X) = log2(TPM(G, X) + PSEUDOCOUNT), TPM(G, X) the mean over the chosen experiment's files (RNA_SELECTION). The measured deviation is D(G, X) = y(G, X) - mean over the thirteen cells X' of y(G, X'): G's level in X relative to its own mean across the reader cells
carried_verbatim.rna_selection: per reader biosample, from the ENCODE portal: every released GRCh38 'gene quantifications' TSV with genome_annotation V29 (the ENCODE4 uniform RNA-seq pipeline, RSEM) of assay 'polyA plus RNA-seq', on the biosample's ontology term name, from a human experiment the portal lists as not perturbed (perturbed=false) and that carries no ERROR audit, and whose file biosample summary names no subcellular fraction, treatment, disease or genetic modification (none of 'fraction', 'treated', 'with ', 'genetically', 'transfected', 'knockdown'). polyA plus is the one assay with such an experiment for all thirteen (SK-N-SH has no whole-cell untreated total RNA-seq in this query). Of the qualifying experiments the one with the most qualifying files is taken, ties broken by the latest date_released and then the lowest accession; the gene's TPM in the biosample is the mean of its TPM over that experiment's qualifying files (its replicates). Chosen from portal metadata alone; no value of any file was read to choose
carried_verbatim.no_rule_baseline: P(G, X) = 0: G's level in X equals its mean over the thirteen reader cells
carried_verbatim.metric: Delta MSE(F, a) = mean over the pairs of D^2 - mean of (D - a*P_F)^2 = mean of (2a*D*P_F - a^2*P_F^2) (combine2.METRIC with the calibrated prediction in place of P), positive when the scaled form's squared error is below the no-rule baseline's. The registered endpoint is this quantity on the HELD-OUT pairs at a = a_F, with a_F fitted on the training pairs. Reported beside it, deciding nothing: the same quantity on the held-out pairs at a = 1 (the uncalibrated form on the held-out genes) and on the training pairs at a = a_F

predictions.form: per form F and gene G, P_F(G, X) for the thirteen cells X: the centred prediction of F's committed genes table, exactly as 7d's and 7h's PREDICTIONS['form'] define it (the gated run's log2 level in X minus its mean over the thirteen cells), rounded to five decimals by the committed table
predictions.calibrated: P_F^a(G, X) = a_F * P_F(G, X), one real number a_F per form and nothing else. No per-gene parameter, no per-cell parameter, no intercept, no transformation of P and no reweighting of pairs or genes: a form's whole calibration is one number, fitted on the training genes alone
predictions.no_rule_baseline: P(G, X) = 0: G's level in X equals its mean over the thirteen reader cells

carried_verbatim.fit: a_F is the one scale that minimises the squared error over the TRAINING pairs of form F, in closed form: a_F = (sum over training pairs of D*P_F) / (sum over training pairs of P_F^2); it is undefined, and the form is NOT_FITTABLE, when the denominator is 0. Equivalently it is the scale that maximises Delta MSE on the training pairs. It is fitted on training pairs only; no held-out value enters it. a_F = 1 is the uncalibrated form, which is what 7d and 7h read
carried_verbatim.control: a within-gene cell permutation, this lane's own and NOT 7d's or 7h's shuffled-reader control (see CARRIED['note']): for each permutation, each gene's thirteen P values are permuted among its own thirteen cells by an independent draw of the seeded generator, every gene keeping its own prediction values, its own range and its own side of the split, and every pair keeping its own D. Only the tie between a prediction and the cell it was made for is broken. The scale is REFITTED on the permuted training pairs and the permuted held-out Delta MSE is computed, so the control asks exactly what the registered endpoint asks of a form whose magnitudes survive and whose cell alignment does not. PERMUTATIONS['count'] permutations at PERMUTATIONS['seed']; control p = (1 + permutations with held-out Delta MSE >= observed) / (1 + count)
carried_verbatim.not_vacuous: a scale fitted to near 0 makes the calibrated prediction near-identical to the no-rule baseline, so its held-out Delta MSE comes out near 0 and the interval straddles 0. A dead scale can therefore MANUFACTURE A STRADDLE but it cannot manufacture a win: a held-out interval wholly above 0 requires the scaled prediction to lower the squared error on genes that entered no fit, which a prediction shrunk to nothing cannot do. 'better' is the one reading the vacuity trap cannot fake, which is why the held-out interval decides and the scale interval is what tells a dead-scale straddle (CALIBRATION_REMOVES, a negative) from a live-scale straddle (INCONCLUSIVE)

outcomes.NOT_TESTABLE: {form}: not testable at the registered size; {g} held-out genes, fewer than the registered {min}; no comparison was read ({scale})
outcomes.BETTER: {form}: better; on genes held out of the fit, the reader-gated run scaled by the one factor fitted on the training genes lowered the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types below the no-rule baseline's, so it is closer to measured RNA than the no-rule baseline (held-out Delta MSE {d} [{ci} {lo}, {hi}] over {n} gene-cell pairs, {g} genes; control p = {p}; {scale})
outcomes.WORSE: {form}: worse; on genes held out of the fit, the reader-gated run scaled by the one factor fitted on the training genes raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's, so it is further from measured RNA than the no-rule baseline even at its best single magnitude (held-out Delta MSE {d} [{ci} {lo}, {hi}] over {n} gene-cell pairs, {g} genes; control p = {p}; {scale})
outcomes.CALIBRATION_REMOVES: {form}: calibration removes the rules: no magnitude of the compiled rules improves on no rule; the held-out interval straddles 0 and the training-set scale interval includes 0, so the calibration is not distinguishable from switching the compiled rules off (held-out Delta MSE {d} [{ci} {lo}, {hi}] over {n} gene-cell pairs, {g} genes; control p = {p}; {scale}). This is a negative result and is not 'no difference detected'
outcomes.INCONCLUSIVE: {form}: inconclusive; the held-out interval straddles 0 while the training-set scale interval excludes 0, so a magnitude is estimated and this measurement does not resolve whether the scaled run is closer to or further from measured RNA than the no-rule baseline (held-out Delta MSE {d} [{ci} {lo}, {hi}] over {n} gene-cell pairs, {g} genes; control p = {p}; {scale})
outcomes.HARNESS_DEFECT: stopped before anything was split, fitted or read: the committed genes tables did not reproduce their committed readings' numbers ({what})

scale_clauses.fitted: fitted scale {a} [{ci} {alo}, {ahi}], one number for the whole form, fitted on {tg} training genes ({tn} gene-cell pairs) and applied unchanged to the held-out genes; the uncalibrated size 7d and 7h read is 1
scale_clauses.negative: the rules point the wrong way on average: the scale that best fits the training genes is negative (scale {a} [{ci} {alo}, {ahi}], fitted on {tg} training genes), so the measured level moves against the compiled prediction
scale_clauses.not_fittable: no scale is defined: the training pairs carry no prediction variance (sum of P^2 is 0)

carried_verbatim.bootstrap_unit: gene: genes are resampled with replacement and carry all thirteen of their pairs
carried_verbatim.note: the endpoint, the no-rule baseline, Delta MSE, the closed-form fit, the gene bootstrap, the within-gene cell permutation control, MIN_GENES, the four-way decision table and EVERY reading word are 7d's, 7h's and M2h's, carried HERE WORD FOR WORD and imported from genomeos/attribution/magcal.py, which this lane does not edit. The population is 7h's, gene for gene: this lane defines no population of its own, admits no gene 7h did not admit and drops none it did. The ONLY thing this lane changes is the SPLIT: by chromosome instead of by sha256 of the gene symbol. Nothing else moves

population: exactly the population of 7h's committed result, gene for gene and in the committed order: the multiplicative composition's 16,509 genes, each with its thirteen (gene, cell) pairs (214,617 pairs). 7h's POPULATION is carried unchanged and so is M2h's choice of it; this lane applies no filter of its own. The rows are read from the committed genes table of data/results/multrna_result.json (pinned by sha256), which carries, per gene, its chromosome and the thirteen P and thirteen D the committed registered reading was computed from. Every one of the 16,509 genes is held out in exactly one of the two folds and is in the training side of exactly one
prior_exposure: STATED PLAINLY, AND NOT A CAVEAT ADDED AFTERWARDS. This is a RE-ANALYSIS of a measurement already read, not a fresh test. The same ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the same thirteen reader biosamples, under the same log2(TPM+1) endpoint and the same no-rule baseline, has already been read by: item 7 (M2b, lane-readercompile) including its post-hoc information term; item 7d (M2c, lane-combine2) for the runtime's mean and promoter competition; item 7h (M2f, lane-multrna) for the multiplicative composition; the capped-sum census (lane-capsumrna), which reached NOT_TESTABLE; M2h (lane-magcal), which fitted the one scale and read 'better' on a random split; and M2i (lane-freshrna), which replicated it with nothing fitted on RNA fresh to this project. The P and D re-split here ARE 7h's committed rows, which are the rows M2h calibrated, so EVERY value this lane reads has been read before -- and the chromosome split was chosen BECAUSE M2h's random split read 'better' and a random split can leak. The chromosome split limits that exposure and does not eliminate it: the partition is fixed by this registration before any held-out number is read and no held-out gene enters its fold's fit, but every gene's RNA value was in M2h's population, the endpoint and baseline were chosen with those readings in hand, and nothing here is a blind prediction of an unseen measurement. Any reading from this lane therefore holds as a statement about THIS measurement's dependence on the split, and is not independent confirmation of M2h; it is the leakage audit of M2h and nothing more
split: by CHROMOSOME, which is the one thing this lane changes. The 24 chromosomes carrying genes in 7h's committed table are partitioned by the PARITY OF THE CHROMOSOME NUMBER -- a property of the chromosome's NAME and of no measured value, fixed by this registration before any held-out number is read. ODD (eleven chromosomes): chr1, chr3, chr5, chr7, chr9, chr11, chr13, chr15, chr17, chr19, chr21. EVEN AND SEX (thirteen chromosomes): chr2, chr4, chr6, chr8, chr10, chr12, chr14, chr16, chr18, chr20, chr22, chrX, chrY. TWO COMPLEMENTARY FOLDS are registered and both are read, so that neither side is a chosen one: FOLD odd_held trains on EVEN AND SEX and holds out ODD; FOLD even_and_sex_held trains on ODD and holds out EVEN AND SEX. A gene is wholly on one side of a fold, with all thirteen of its pairs: no cell of a held-out gene enters that fold's fit. WHY PARITY: it is nameable in advance, needs no gene count, no RNA value and no fitted number to state, splits the genome into two pieces of comparable size, and puts no chromosome in both. The sex chromosomes are placed with the even autosomes by the one rule that they are not odd-numbered; chrY carries 13 genes and chrX 633, so that placement moves 646 of 16,509 genes and is declared here rather than tuned
which_split_is_whose: M2h's split is NOT re-run as this lane's endpoint and is NOT this lane's split: it is reproduced in the HARNESS only, to prove that this lane reads the same rows through the same functions and gets M2h's committed numbers back. This lane's registered endpoint is read on the chromosome folds alone
refitted: THE SCALE IS REFITTED ON THE TRAINING CHROMOSOMES OF EACH FOLD. It is NOT taken as M2h's constant +0.2146. This is deliberate and is the point of the lane: refitting tests whether the SCALE ITSELF TRANSPORTS from one set of chromosomes to another, which is a property of the compiled rules, rather than testing whether one number fitted on a random half happens to hold -- which is M2h's question and is already answered. Each fold's scale is the closed-form minimiser over that fold's TRAINING pairs alone (magcal.FIT, imported unchanged), bootstrapped on that fold's training genes with the scale refitted on each resample (magcal.bootstrap_scale). No held-out pair enters any fit

fold_words.odd_held: the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024), scale fitted on the even-numbered autosomes and the sex chromosomes and read on the odd-numbered autosomes held out
fold_words.even_and_sex_held: the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024), scale fitted on the odd-numbered autosomes and read on the even-numbered autosomes and the sex chromosomes held out

metric: Delta MSE(F, a) = mean over the pairs of D^2 - mean of (D - a*P_F)^2 = mean of (2a*D*P_F - a^2*P_F^2) (combine2.METRIC with the calibrated prediction in place of P), positive when the scaled form's squared error is below the no-rule baseline's. The registered endpoint is this quantity on the HELD-OUT pairs at a = a_F, with a_F fitted on the training pairs. Carried verbatim from M2h, with the HELD-OUT side now meaning the held-out CHROMOSOMES of the fold instead of the held-out gene symbols
interval: 98.33% percentile interval, magcal.FORM_INTERVAL taken UNCHANGED, DECIDED NOW AND NOT AFTER, for three reasons stated in advance. (1) COMPARABILITY: M2h's committed multiplicative reading is +0.04339 [98.33% CI +0.0379, +0.04894], and the whole point of this lane is to put its own number beside that one, which a different width would make a comparison of widths as well as of effects. (2) MACHINERY: this lane calls magcal.bootstrap_delta and magcal.bootstrap_scale read-only and they read magcal.FORM_INTERVAL; changing the width would mean editing magcal's file or reimplementing its bootstrap, both of which this lane is forbidden to do and both of which would be worse than a conservative width. (3) CONSERVATISM: two folds of one form are judged here, so a Bonferroni correction from 95% over two readings would be 97.5% -- 7d's own two-arm convention. 98.33% is WIDER than that, so using it cannot manufacture an exclusion of 0 that the correct correction would deny. M2h's 98.33% was Bonferroni over its three forms; here the same width is a deliberate over-correction and is labelled as one, never as a Bonferroni over two

bootstrap.unit: gene: genes are resampled with replacement and carry all thirteen of their pairs
bootstrap.interval: per fold, the 98.33% percentile interval (INTERVAL). The held-out Delta MSE interval resamples the HELD-OUT CHROMOSOMES' genes with replacement, each carrying its thirteen pairs, with the scale held fixed at the value fitted on the training chromosomes (magcal.bootstrap_delta); the SCALE interval resamples the TRAINING CHROMOSOMES' genes with replacement, each carrying its thirteen pairs, and refits the scale on each resample (magcal.bootstrap_scale). The unit is the GENE in both, as M2h registered it. A chromosome-level bootstrap is NOT registered as the endpoint's interval and is not computed: with eleven and thirteen chromosomes it would be a resample of eleven or thirteen units, and M2h's gene unit is what is carried verbatim. That the gene unit does not price in between-chromosome correlation is written as a LIMITATION, not read as a result

control: a within-gene cell permutation, this lane's own and NOT 7d's or 7h's shuffled-reader control (see CARRIED['note']): for each permutation, each gene's thirteen P values are permuted among its own thirteen cells by an independent draw of the seeded generator, every gene keeping its own prediction values, its own range and its own side of the split, and every pair keeping its own D. Only the tie between a prediction and the cell it was made for is broken. The scale is REFITTED on the permuted training pairs and the permuted held-out Delta MSE is computed, so the control asks exactly what the registered endpoint asks of a form whose magnitudes survive and whose cell alignment does not. PERMUTATIONS['count'] permutations at PERMUTATIONS['seed']; control p = (1 + permutations with held-out Delta MSE >= observed) / (1 + count). Applied per fold, with that fold's training chromosomes as the training side and its held-out chromosomes as the held-out side; magcal.permuted_control, imported unchanged
harness: before any chromosome split, scale, held-out value or control of this lane is computed, all of the following must hold. (1) the genes table of data/results/multrna_result.json has 7h's committed gene count (16,509) and pair count (214,617); (2) Delta MSE at scale 1 recomputed over all of its pairs equals 7h's committed delta_mse within TOLERANCE; (3) every gene's P and D have thirteen entries, every symbol is non-empty, no symbol occurs twice, and every row's chromosome is non-empty; (4) M2h'S COMMITTED GENE-LEVEL NUMBERS REPRODUCE: applying magcal.split_rows (sha256 of the symbol) and magcal's fit_scale, bootstrap_scale, delta_mse, bootstrap_delta and permuted_control at M2h's registered resamples, seeds and permutation count returns M2h's committed training gene count (8,181), held-out gene count (8,328), fitted scale, scale interval, held-out Delta MSE, held-out interval, control p and outcome (BETTER) -- counts and outcome exactly, every real number within M2H_TOLERANCE; (5) every chromosome in the table falls in exactly one of this lane's two chromosome sets, the two sets are disjoint, their union is the table's chromosomes, and the two folds' held-out gene counts sum to the table's gene count. A miss in ANY of them stops the run (HARNESS_DEFECT) and nothing is split by chromosome, fitted or read. (4) is the check that makes every later difference attributable to the SPLIT and to nothing else: same rows, same functions, same seeds, M2h's numbers back

transport.SURVIVES_BOTH_FOLDS: M2h's scale SURVIVES a chromosome-held-out split: on both complementary chromosome folds, with the scale refitted on the training chromosomes, the scaled multiplicative composition is closer to measured RNA than the no-rule baseline on chromosomes that entered no fit, so the gain is not an artefact of a random split leaking through shared compiled elements. It remains about 2% of the variance
transport.SURVIVES_ONE_FOLD: M2h's scale DOES NOT TRANSPORT CLEANLY ACROSS CHROMOSOMES: it reads better on one of the two complementary chromosome folds and not on the other, so the gain M2h measured on a random split of gene symbols is REGIONAL and is NOT shown to be free of leakage through shared compiled elements. This is a weakness in M2h's one positive result and is stated as one
transport.DOES_NOT_SURVIVE: M2h's scale DOES NOT SURVIVE a chromosome-held-out split: on NEITHER complementary chromosome fold, with the scale refitted on the training chromosomes, is the scaled multiplicative composition shown closer to measured RNA than the no-rule baseline on chromosomes that entered no fit. M2h's gain is therefore at least partly a LEAK through compiled elements shared between its training and held-out genes, which its random split did not exclude. This is the consequential outcome and it is not softened

transport_rule: the transport verdict is a function of the two folds' outcomes and of nothing else, fixed here: both folds BETTER -> SURVIVES_BOTH_FOLDS; exactly one fold BETTER -> SURVIVES_ONE_FOLD; neither fold BETTER -> DOES_NOT_SURVIVE. A fold that is NOT_TESTABLE or NOT_FITTABLE counts as not BETTER and is named in the reading with its own registered sentence. The transport verdict NEVER overrides a fold's own sentence: both folds' registered sentences are reported in FOLDS order whatever the transport verdict is
magnitude_comparison: reported beside each fold's reading and DECIDING NOTHING: the fold's held-out Delta MSE and fitted scale against M2h's committed gene-level +0.04339 [98.33% CI +0.0379, +0.04894] and +0.2146 [+0.2007, +0.2283]. THE RULE, FIXED NOW AND NOT AFTER: if two intervals OVERLAP, the honest reading is CONSISTENT WITH THE SAME EFFECT, and neither 'stronger', 'weaker', 'strengthened' nor 'weakened' may be said; only a fold interval lying WHOLLY BELOW M2h's lower bound may be read as the chromosome split giving a SMALLER number than the random split, and wholly above as a LARGER one. The two populations are NOT independent -- they are the same 16,509 genes repartitioned -- so no test of the difference is registered and none will be computed
decision: 1. If the HARNESS misses on any of its five points, the run stops before anything of this lane is split, fitted or read (HARNESS_DEFECT), and no chromosome-fold scale and no held-out value is computed. 2. Per fold, the scale is REFITTED on the fold's training chromosomes alone (REFITTED, FIT) and reported with its 98.33% training-gene bootstrap interval (refitted on each resample) in every reading, whatever the reading is; a training denominator of 0 is NOT_FITTABLE and the fold is read no further. 3. Per fold, fewer than MIN_GENES held-out genes is NOT_TESTABLE and no comparison is read. 4. Otherwise the fold's verdict is M2h's WHICH_GOVERNS four-way table, applied as written by magcal.decide, on the held-out Delta MSE at the refitted scale with its 98.33% held-out-gene bootstrap interval (the scale fixed): lower bound > 0 -> BETTER; upper bound < 0 -> WORSE (the falsifier); straddles 0 and the scale interval includes 0 -> CALIBRATION_REMOVES, a negative; straddles 0 and the scale interval excludes 0 -> INCONCLUSIVE. 5. A negative scale is reported BESIDE whichever of those applies, in SCALE_CLAUSES['negative']'s words, never instead of it. 6. The control p is reported in every fold sentence and changes no verdict. 7. The transport verdict is TRANSPORT_RULE applied to the two folds' outcomes. 8. The registered reading is: the transport sentence FIRST, then the two folds' registered sentences in FOLDS order joined by '; ', then MAGNITUDE_COMPARISON's finding, then PRIOR_EXPOSURE_CLAUSE, always
falsifier: the reading under test is M2h's, that one scale on the compiled rules' multiplicative composition brings the run closer to measured RNA on data that entered no fit, and that this is a property of the rules rather than of a random split. It is FALSIFIED for a fold when that fold's held-out Delta MSE interval excludes 0 on the BASELINE's side (upper bound < 0, outcome WORSE): with the scale refitted freely on the training chromosomes, the form is still further from measured RNA than running no rule at all on chromosomes that entered no fit. An interval STRADDLING 0 falsifies nothing and is read by the scale, exactly as M2h registered: CALIBRATION_REMOVES when the scale interval includes 0 -- 'calibration removes the rules', A NEGATIVE AND NOT 'no difference detected' -- and INCONCLUSIVE when the scale interval excludes 0, meaning a magnitude is estimated and this measurement does not resolve the comparison. 'INCONCLUSIVE' is therefore exactly one case here: a live scale with a straddling held-out interval, and it is the one case from which nothing is concluded in either direction. An interval excluding 0 on the rules' side (BETTER) is a positive for that fold. ACROSS the folds, the thing being falsified is TRANSPORT: anything other than BETTER on BOTH folds means M2h's gain is not shown to survive a split that cannot leak through shared elements, and SURVIVES_ONE_FOLD and DOES_NOT_SURVIVE both say so in their own registered words. NOT_VACUOUS, carried from M2h, states why 'better' is the one reading a dead scale cannot fake
prior_exposure_clause: carried with every reading: this RNA is not a fresh measurement. limitations: PRIOR EXPOSURE, first because it is the largest: see PRIOR_EXPOSURE. These are the rows M2h calibrated and 7h, 7d and item 7 read before it. the bootstrap unit is the GENE, carried verbatim from M2h, so the held-out interval prices in variation between genes and NOT between chromosomes. With eleven and thirteen chromosomes a chromosome-level resample was considered and deliberately NOT registered, because changing M2h's unit would change more than the split. A fold interval is therefore narrower than one that priced in between-chromosome correlation would be, and the post-hoc per-chromosome scales are reported so that a reader can see that spread directly

a chromosome split removes element sharing AND regional structure at once. A drop from M2h's number is evidence that M2h's random split is not clean, but it does not apportion the drop between element leakage and genuine regional variation in the scale, and nothing here attempts to

two folds of one form are read and the interval is 98.33%, wider than a Bonferroni over two would require. That is conservative for exclusion of 0 and it is NOT conservative for a straddle: an over-wide interval makes CALIBRATION_REMOVES and INCONCLUSIVE easier to reach than the correct correction would. Both directions of that are stated here in advance

one scale is the smallest calibration there is and also the weakest: it can only shrink, grow or flip the predictions as a block, and cannot fix a form whose error is in the SHAPE of its prediction across cells or across genes. Carried from M2h
the calibration is a statistical rescaling and not a mechanism; nothing here attributes the size to any stage of the compiled pipeline. Carried from M2h
the P and D are the committed table's five-decimal roundings, which is why the harness admits TOLERANCE rather than exact equality. Carried from M2h

chromosomes are disjoint in element membership BY CONSTRUCTION of the compiler (one program per chromosome, cis targets). That is a property of the compiled programs and not of biology: it says nothing about whether a real regulatory element can act between chromosomes, and if a future compiler emitted a trans rule WHY_STRONGER would no longer hold
accessibility is not function, and an emitted target is a model attribution and never a measured regulatory relationship. Carried forward unchanged
post_hoc: reported beside the registered reading, DECIDING NOTHING and able to change no verdict: (1) THE PER-CHROMOSOME SCALES -- for each of the 24 chromosomes, the one scale fitted on THAT CHROMOSOME'S GENES ALONE with its gene and pair count, so a reader can see whether the magnitude is uniform or regional; (2) for each of the 24 chromosomes, the scale fitted on the OTHER 23 (a leave-one-chromosome-out training scale) beside its own, which is what a 24-fold version of this lane would have fitted; (3) the spread of (1): its minimum, maximum, median and interquartile range, and how many of the 24 lie inside M2h's committed scale interval. A chromosome with fewer than MIN_GENES genes is reported with its count and FLAGGED as below the registered floor -- chrY carries 13 genes in 7h's table -- and no chromosome-level scale is read as a verdict about that chromosome. None of (1), (2) or (3) is a test: no interval is placed on a per-chromosome scale and no comparison between chromosomes is registered
descriptives: per fold, deciding nothing: the held-out Delta MSE at scale 1 (the uncalibrated form on the held-out chromosomes) with its 98.33% interval; the training Delta MSE at the refitted scale and at 1; the training and held-out gene and pair counts; mean(D^2), mean(P^2), mean(scale^2 P^2) and mean(D*P) on each side, so the size the calibration keeps is visible as a number; the held-out Delta MSE per reader cell; the predicted range quantiles before and after scaling; the control's median and 95th percentile

seven_h_verbatim.reading: the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024): worse; the reader-gated run of genes with two or more compiled elements raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.5361 [97.5% CI -0.5637, -0.5088] over 214,617 gene-cell pairs, 16,509 genes; control p = 1). Head-to-head over the 2,405 genes in all three populations (31,265 gene-cell pairs), the multiplicative composition was closer to measured RNA than the runtime's mean (MSE(mean) - MSE(multiplicative) +0.04395 [97.5% CI +0.0385, +0.04979]) and closer to measured RNA than the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter) (MSE(competition) - MSE(multiplicative) +0.7383 [97.5% CI +0.6625, +0.8183]).

m2h_verbatim.reading: the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024): better; on genes held out of the fit, the reader-gated run scaled by the one factor fitted on the training genes lowered the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types below the no-rule baseline's, so it is closer to measured RNA than the no-rule baseline (held-out Delta MSE +0.04339 [98.33% CI +0.0379, +0.04894] over 108,264 gene-cell pairs, 8,328 genes; control p = 0.000999; fitted scale +0.2146 [98.33% CI +0.2007, +0.2283], one number for the whole form, fitted on 8,181 training genes (106,353 gene-cell pairs) and applied unchanged to the held-out genes; the uncalibrated size 7d and 7h read is 1)

decisions: WHY THIS LANE EXISTS: M2h's one positive result is split by sha256 of the gene SYMBOL -- a RANDOM split. Genes that share a compiled element are not independent, which M2i's own post hoc acknowledged by reporting a 1-Mb locus-cluster interval beside its gene-level one, so a training gene and a held-out gene may be fitted through the same element and 'held out' is weaker than it sounds. This lane re-splits the same rows by CHROMOSOME, which cannot leak that way, and reads M2h's endpoint again

design: M2h's, with ONE thing changed and nothing else. The endpoint, the no-rule baseline, Delta MSE, the closed-form fit, the gene bootstrap, the within-gene cell permutation control, MIN_GENES, the four-way decision table and every reading word are imported from genomeos/attribution/magcal.py and carried verbatim; the population is 7h's, gene for gene. The ONE change is the split

one form, not three: the multiplicative composition, which is M2h's arm that read 'better'. The two arms that read 'worse' at their best scale are not re-split, because there is no positive result there to audit for leakage

THE SCALE IS REFITTED on each fold's training chromosomes and is NOT taken as M2h's constant +0.2146. That is deliberate: refitting tests whether the SCALE TRANSPORTS between chromosome sets, a property of the compiled rules, rather than whether one number fitted on a random half happens to hold, which is M2h's own question and is already answered

split: by chromosome, by the PARITY OF THE CHROMOSOME NAME, with TWO COMPLEMENTARY FOLDS both read so that neither side is a chosen one. Parity needs no gene count, no RNA value and no fitted number to state, and puts no chromosome in both sides. The sex chromosomes go with the even autosomes by the one rule that they are not odd-numbered -- 646 of 16,509 genes, declared rather than tuned

interval: 98.33%, magcal.FORM_INTERVAL unchanged, decided now. It keeps the number directly comparable to M2h's committed +0.04339 [98.33% CI +0.0379, +0.04894]; it is what magcal's bootstrap functions compute, and this lane calls them read-only rather than editing magcal or reimplementing its bootstrap; and it is WIDER than the 97.5% a Bonferroni over this lane's two folds would require (7d's two-arm convention), so it cannot manufacture an exclusion of 0. It is labelled a deliberate over-correction and never a Bonferroni over two
control: M2h's own within-gene cell permutation, applied per fold with the scale refitted on the permuted training chromosomes. It is reported in every fold sentence and changes no verdict

the decision procedure is M2h's WHICH_GOVERNS, the supervisor's science ruling of 2026-10-10, carried verbatim and applied by magcal.decide: the held-out interval decides, and the scale interval only splits the straddle case -- a scale interval including 0 with a straddling held-out interval reads 'calibration removes the rules', A NEGATIVE. Above it, this lane's own TRANSPORT_RULE is fixed here: both folds BETTER -> SURVIVES_BOTH_FOLDS, one fold -> SURVIVES_ONE_FOLD, neither -> DOES_NOT_SURVIVE, and the transport sentence is read FIRST so that a failure to transport cannot be buried

the per-chromosome scales are POST HOC and decide nothing: no interval is placed on one and no comparison between chromosomes is registered. They are reported so a reader can see whether the magnitude is uniform or regional, with chrY's 13 genes flagged as below MIN_GENES

parameters.split: by CHROMOSOME, which is the one thing this lane changes. The 24 chromosomes carrying genes in 7h's committed table are partitioned by the PARITY OF THE CHROMOSOME NUMBER -- a property of the chromosome's NAME and of no measured value, fixed by this registration before any held-out number is read. ODD (eleven chromosomes): chr1, chr3, chr5, chr7, chr9, chr11, chr13, chr15, chr17, chr19, chr21. EVEN AND SEX (thirteen chromosomes): chr2, chr4, chr6, chr8, chr10, chr12, chr14, chr16, chr18, chr20, chr22, chrX, chrY. TWO COMPLEMENTARY FOLDS are registered and both are read, so that neither side is a chosen one: FOLD odd_held trains on EVEN AND SEX and holds out ODD; FOLD even_and_sex_held trains on ODD and holds out EVEN AND SEX. A gene is wholly on one side of a fold, with all thirteen of its pairs: no cell of a held-out gene enters that fold's fit. WHY PARITY: it is nameable in advance, needs no gene count, no RNA value and no fitted number to state, splits the genome into two pieces of comparable size, and puts no chromosome in both. The sex chromosomes are placed with the even autosomes by the one rule that they are not odd-numbered; chrY carries 13 genes and chrX 633, so that placement moves 646 of 16,509 genes and is declared here rather than tuned
parameters.refitted: THE SCALE IS REFITTED ON THE TRAINING CHROMOSOMES OF EACH FOLD. It is NOT taken as M2h's constant +0.2146. This is deliberate and is the point of the lane: refitting tests whether the SCALE ITSELF TRANSPORTS from one set of chromosomes to another, which is a property of the compiled rules, rather than testing whether one number fitted on a random half happens to hold -- which is M2h's question and is already answered. Each fold's scale is the closed-form minimiser over that fold's TRAINING pairs alone (magcal.FIT, imported unchanged), bootstrapped on that fold's training genes with the scale refitted on each resample (magcal.bootstrap_scale). No held-out pair enters any fit
parameters.interval_decision: 98.33% percentile interval, magcal.FORM_INTERVAL taken UNCHANGED, DECIDED NOW AND NOT AFTER, for three reasons stated in advance. (1) COMPARABILITY: M2h's committed multiplicative reading is +0.04339 [98.33% CI +0.0379, +0.04894], and the whole point of this lane is to put its own number beside that one, which a different width would make a comparison of widths as well as of effects. (2) MACHINERY: this lane calls magcal.bootstrap_delta and magcal.bootstrap_scale read-only and they read magcal.FORM_INTERVAL; changing the width would mean editing magcal's file or reimplementing its bootstrap, both of which this lane is forbidden to do and both of which would be worse than a conservative width. (3) CONSERVATISM: two folds of one form are judged here, so a Bonferroni correction from 95% over two readings would be 97.5% -- 7d's own two-arm convention. 98.33% is WIDER than that, so using it cannot manufacture an exclusion of 0 that the correct correction would deny. M2h's 98.33% was Bonferroni over its three forms; here the same width is a deliberate over-correction and is labelled as one, never as a Bonferroni over two

bootstrap.unit: gene: genes are resampled with replacement and carry all thirteen of their pairs
bootstrap.interval: per fold, the 98.33% percentile interval (INTERVAL). The held-out Delta MSE interval resamples the HELD-OUT CHROMOSOMES' genes with replacement, each carrying its thirteen pairs, with the scale held fixed at the value fitted on the training chromosomes (magcal.bootstrap_delta); the SCALE interval resamples the TRAINING CHROMOSOMES' genes with replacement, each carrying its thirteen pairs, and refits the scale on each resample (magcal.bootstrap_scale). The unit is the GENE in both, as M2h registered it. A chromosome-level bootstrap is NOT registered as the endpoint's interval and is not computed: with eleven and thirteen chromosomes it would be a resample of eleven or thirteen units, and M2h's gene unit is what is carried verbatim. That the gene unit does not price in between-chromosome correlation is written as a LIMITATION, not read as a result

parameters.free_parameters: one real scale per fold; no per-gene and no per-cell parameter
